lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: Hey Dex... why does Heinz ketchup say *{57|fifty-seven}* on the bottle?

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: Wait, don't tell me. It's {57|fifty-seven} *tomatoes.* Squished into every bottle.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: Kip... no. That number's basically *made up.* And it hides a *trick.*

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: In {1896|eighteen ninety-six}, Henry Heinz saw an ad on a train: *{21|twenty-one} styles* of shoes.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: He loved it. So he gave his company a number too: *{57|fifty-seven} varieties.*

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: And nobody's totally sure why he picked {57|fifty-seven}.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: But here's the best part. On glass bottles, that *{57|fifty-seven}* is where Heinz says to *tap.* One firm tap there, and the ketchup comes out way easier.

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: I've been slapping the *bottom* my whole life.

lines.speaker: kip
lines.text: Okay, but seriously... why {57|fifty-seven}? Drop your theory in the *comments*.
